claims.text: Attachment failures route through the CliError contract: an unreadable or missing path fails before login, more than 10 files is rejected client-side, and a Discord 413 (size) is mapped to a typed error naming the size sent — each exits 1 with a remediation and no traceback reaches stderr.

hard_questions.text: What size limit does the pre-flight check enforce, given the real cap depends on the guild's boost tier? Options: hard-code the 8 MiB unboosted floor (rejects valid uploads on boosted guilds), fetch the guild to read its tier (an extra round trip and a guild id the message verbs do not currently take), or skip the pre-flight and map Discord's 413 cleanly.
hard_questions.resolution: USER: no size pre-flight. Only Discord knows the guild's real cap, so upload and map the HTTP 413 into a CliError naming the size sent and Discord's own message. The 10-attachment count cap is still asserted client-side (it is a fixed documented limit); the size cap is not guessed.

claims.instruction: Per the q2 decision: no size pre-flight — os.stat only to prove the path is readable, never to guess a limit. The 10-attachment count IS asserted client-side (fixed documented Discord limit). The size case is discord.HTTPException status 413 mapped in discord_client.run's existing handler chain, with the byte count we sent in the message. Assert exit code and the 'error:'/'hint:' stderr shape in tests, not just the message text.

hard_questions.text: What does --after/--since accept: an ISO 8601 timestamp, a relative duration like '90d', or a message-id snowflake? discord.py's history(after=) takes a datetime or a Snowflake-ish object; the CLI has to pick a surface and say so.
hard_questions.resolution: USER: accept both an ISO 8601 timestamp and a relative duration ('90d'), and accept a partial timestamp — a date-only '2026-06-01' is valid and means midnight UTC that day. Durations are resolved CLI-side to now - delta and handed to discord.py's history(after=<datetime>).

hard_questions.text: risk: 'channel messages' currently validates --limit into [1,100]. Once paging exists, that ceiling means two different things depending on whether a window was given — a subtle contract change worth stating explicitly rather than leaving implicit.

Options: --limit caps the paged result (a windowed read can still truncate, and the coverage signal reports it), --limit is rejected as mutually exclusive with a window, or --limit is silently ignored once a window is given. The spec currently says only that the 1-100 validation is kept 'for the no-window case'.
hard_questions.resolution: USER: --limit caps a windowed read as a safety ceiling, and the coverage signal reports that the window was not fully covered, naming what stopped it (limit vs window end). Gives a bounded first scan of a huge channel — the unbounded-walk worry in h4.

hard_questions.text: What is the process exit code when a batch resolves some ids and fails others? Per-id error entries mean the run is neither a clean success nor a failure: 0 (the batch ran, inspect the entries), 1 (something the user asked for did not resolve), or a new partial code. The exit contract today is 0 ok / 1 user error / 2 env error / 3+ reserved.
hard_questions.resolution: USER: exit 0 with per-id error entries. The batch ran as asked; an unresolvable id is data, not a CLI failure — a deleted account must not make a 200-id scan report failure. Callers inspect the entries, which they must do anyway.

hard_questions.text: What does the human (non --json) rendering of a multi-id 'user get' look like, and is per-id output order guaranteed to match input order? A consumer joining names back onto aggregated author ids needs stable ordering or must key on the id field.

open_vagueness.resolution: ANSWERED LIVE (2026-09-04): Discord CDN attachment URLs DO carry signed expiry parameters — ?ex= (expiry), &is= (issued), &hm= (signature). scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / data-flow lens: discord.py 2.7.1 before/after naive-datetime handling
scope_entries.finding: A naive datetime is interpreted as LOCAL time, so the confirmed 'midnight UTC' reading of a date-only --since holds only if the CLI attaches tzinfo itself.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / durability lens: discord.py 2.7.1 Attachment attributes
scope_entries.finding: url 404s once the message is deleted and proxy_url may last only minutes; whether the CDN URL also carries signed expiry was NOT checked (no live upload made this pass) and is parked unverified rather than asserted.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / migration lens: persistent state
scope_entries.finding: Clean pass — the CLI holds no persistent store, no schema, and no on-disk state to migrate; the only cross-version compatibility surface is the 'user get' output shape, already routed as c30.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / concurrency lens: the one-shot transport
scope_entries.finding: Clean pass for in-process concurrency — each verb is a single asyncio.run with one client, no shared mutable state, no locking need. The residual concern is external, not internal: the channel keeps receiving messages while a page walk runs (parked).

obligations.seam: message post / message reply / thread post argparse + send
obligations.behavior: a repeatable, order-preserving --file attaches every file to ONE send, and content is optional once at least one file is given
obligations.source_text: 'message post', 'message reply' and 'thread post' accept a repeatable, order-preserving --file PATH; the positional content becomes optional once at least one --file is given (an attachment-only message is valid on Discord).

obligations.behavior: a missing/unreadable/directory path and an 11th file each raise CliError with a remediation before login; no OSError or builtin ValueError escapes
obligations.source_text: Attachment failures route through the CliError contract: an unreadable or missing path fails before login, more than 10 files is rejected client-side, and a Discord 413 (size) is mapped to a typed error naming the size sent — each exits 1 with a remediation and no traceback reaches stderr.

obligations.seam: the --json attachments payload on post/reply/thread post
obligations.behavior: the created message's attachments are reported as [{id, filename, url, size}] under the key 'attachments'
obligations.source_text: --json on post/reply/thread-post includes the resulting attachment ids and URLs alongside the message id, so a caller can reference what it uploaded.

obligations.seam: channel messages --since window walk and coverage signal
obligations.behavior: a window pages past the 100-message cap, --limit caps it as a ceiling, and every --json run carries a window signal naming what stopped the walk
obligations.source_text: 'channel messages' gains a time-window option (--after/--since) that pages past the 100-message cap, and its --json payload carries an explicit signal for whether the requested window was fully covered.

obligations.behavior: author.bot and author.global_name are returned for every message with no extra fetch_user call
obligations.source_text: _message_dict() gains author.bot and author.global_name, matching the fields 'user get' already returns.

obligations.behavior: many ids resolve in one login session in input order, --json is always an array, and a per-id failure yields an error entry while the process exits 0
obligations.source_text: 'user get' takes one or more ids (varargs, plus --ids-file with '-' for stdin), resolves them all inside one discord_client.run() session, and always emits a JSON array — including for a single id. Resolution is tolerant per id: an unresolvable id yields an error entry instead of failing the batch.

obligations.behavior: no top-level third-party import anywhere in the runtime package and dependencies == []
obligations.source_text: Zero runtime dependencies is unchanged: discord.File and everything else new stays behind discord_client.require_discord()'s lazy import under the [discord] extra. tests/test_no_runtime_deps.py still passes untouched.

obligations.seam: channel messages ordering across both read modes
obligations.behavior: output is oldest-first for a windowed read AND a plain read, never relying on history()'s context-dependent oldest_first default
obligations.source_text: The paged read must emit oldest-first regardless of whether a window was given: discord.py's history() sets oldest_first=True by default when after= is passed, so channel.py's existing unconditional collected.reverse() would silently flip a windowed read into newest-first — the opposite of the documented 'oldest first, the natural reading order' contract.

obligations.behavior: every accepted --since form returns a timezone-aware UTC instant, identical under any host TZ
obligations.source_text: Every datetime handed to history() must be timezone-aware UTC. discord.py treats a NAIVE datetime as LOCAL time, so the confirmed q3 decision that a date-only '--since 2026-06-01' means midnight UTC is only true if the CLI attaches tzinfo itself.

obligations.behavior: an HTTPException with status 413 becomes a CliError whose remediation names the boost-tier dependence, exiting 1 with the error:/hint: stderr shape
obligations.source_text: Attachment argument errors must be caught by the verb, not left to discord_client.run's handler chain: discord.File(path) raises OSError on an unreadable path and Messageable.send raises ValueError (files list too long) and TypeError — none of which are discord.* exceptions, so run()'s mapping misses them and they fall through to the generic catch-all, losing the typed remediation c13 promises.

obligations.behavior: all three self-teaching surfaces describe the shipped flags, including --ids-file in learn's JSON payload
obligations.source_text: The self-teaching surfaces stay true: explain/catalog.py entries, learn.py (_TEXT and _as_json_payload) and overview.py (_VERBS) all describe the new flags.

obligations.behavior: the CLI itself tells an agent that --file is an unsandboxed local read with no path allow-listing, before it uses the flag
obligations.source_text: --file performs an unsandboxed local read: any path the invoking process can open is uploaded to a third party. The CLI does not restrict paths, and it is not a confused-deputy guard — an agent handed a path uploads whatever is there. The operator owns which paths reach the flag.

obligations.behavior: the docs state that live tests leave permanent artifacts because there is no delete verb, and must target a sandbox channel
obligations.source_text: Posting is irreversible on this surface: there is no delete verb, so every message and every attachment this CLI creates — including live-test artifacts in the sandbox channel — is permanent as far as this tool is concerned. Removal is a manual Discord action.

obligations.behavior: the CLI states an attachment URL is a reference that 404s once the message is deleted, not durable storage
obligations.source_text: An attachment URL returned in --json is a reference, not durable storage: discord.py documents that Attachment.url 404s once the message is deleted, and proxy_url may survive only minutes. Callers must not treat the URL as an archive of the file they uploaded.
